brief.title: How memory fails on stage
brief.goal: Students practice talks out loud instead of rereading notes.
brief.audience: Sixty second-year psychology students who prepare by rereading slides.
brief.bigIdea: Recall practice protects memory under stress while rereading does not.

points.text: Stress blocks retrieval of reread material

points.example: Retrieval practice beat rereading by 50% after one week
Three short sessions beat one long session

brief.openingLine: Think of the last time your mind went blank in front of a room.
brief.closingLine: Before your next talk, close the slides and say it out loud three times.

issues.problem: Point three, on spacing, does not connect back to the stress versus rereading claim in the big idea.
issues.action: Cut point three, or rewrite it to show how spacing helps recall specifically under stress.

issues.problem: These students reread because it feels easy and familiar, but the brief never names that feeling.
issues.action: Add a line stating that rereading feels productive even though it does not build real recall.
